queuelet: fix experiment 03 findings; add checks (lesson 03)

Experiment 03 (Vary it) filed eight reports; the reconciliation made them
unplanned U11-U18. All eight are fixed here. The planned E03 defects
(D05-D08, D26) were fixed in E01 and held.

Flaws, all at explore-it/lesson-02:
- U11 the decoder read one JSON value and stopped: trailing data and a
  second object got 201, invalid UTF-8 was rewritten (api.go:53).
- U12 member names matched case-insensitively: KIND, LEASE_TOKEN counted.
- U13 delay, nack delay and heartbeat extension overflowed time.Duration:
  "later" became "now" (enqueue.go:54, nack.go:24, jobs.go:84).
- U14 out-of-range settings and long names came back 409 / 500 with
  driver text (queues.go:48, :94).
- U15 one queue's retention_hours >= ~6e7 made the global Retain statement
  fail every tick for every namespace; /health 503 (expire.go:66).
- U16 Backoff overflowed: attempt 32 at base 5 retried at once (jobs.go:21).
- U17 backoff.max_seconds was stored and never applied.
- U18 PATCH {"webhook":{"secret":…}} cleared the URL, and vice versa.

Fix: one strict decoder (whole body, UTF-8, one object, exact member
names); jobs.MaxSeconds = 2147483647 bounds every seconds field and
max_attempts; saturating Backoff honouring max_seconds; queue validation
before the store (names 1-128, limits in range, retention <= 1e6 h; only
a unique violation is 409); Retain compares elapsed hours so no stored
value can overflow it; webhook PATCH merges member by member.

Spec decisions (SPEC.md, register/reconciliations/03.md): a command body
is one UTF-8 JSON object with exact member names; seconds fields and
max_attempts <= 2147483647; names 1-128 chars, only a taken name is 409;
retention 0-1000000 h; max_seconds >= base_seconds caps each wait and a
computed wait never precedes the failure; webhook PATCH is member-wise.
A1 (a default cap) stays with E04: its control is still PRESENT.

  integration checks 54/54; unit tests pass.

queuelet: fix experiment 04 findings; resolve A1; add checks (lesson 04)

Experiment 04 (Judge it) wrote thirteen Never/Always rules before probing
and filed five reports; the reconciliation made them unplanned U19-U23.
All five are fixed here, and the A1 spec silence is decided. The planned
E04 defects (D09-D11, D25) were fixed in E01; D09-D11 held as rules here.

Flaws, all at explore-it/lesson-03:
- U19 requests no route serves got Go's plain-text 404/405, outside the
  error form (api.go:172).
- U20 attempt rows copied jobs.attempts, so after dead -> retry -> ack two
  executions shared n=1 (ack.go:14, nack.go:30).
- U21 negative delay_seconds was accepted on enqueue and nack: -5 put the
  retry before the failure, -9223372037 wrapped to 2322 (jobs.go:67,
  enqueue.go:55).
- U22 heartbeat/ack/nack ignored lease_expires_at, so an expired lease won
  until the 1 s sweep ran (ack.go:10, nack.go:14, jobs.go:97).
- U23 release by expiry or worker deletion kept run_at, so queued age
  counted the leased time (expire.go:41, api/jobs.go:126).
- A1 without backoff.max_seconds, attempt 20 at base 5 waited 30 days.

Fix: an `unmatched` fallback writes not_found / method_not_allowed in the
envelope (Allow kept); attempt n = rows so far + 1; delay_seconds 0..2^31-1;
`lease_expires_at > now` in the three worker guards; run_at = now on
release; jobs.DefaultMaxSeconds = 3600 (or the base, if larger).

Spec decisions (SPEC.md, register/reconciliations/04.md): unmatched path
404 / method 405 in the error form; delay_seconds is never negative; attempt
n numbers every execution across retries while attempts/attempt still reset;
a lease ends at lease_expires_at with no grace period; a released job is
ready at the release; default backoff cap 3600 s or base_seconds if larger.

Checks: TestL04U19..U23, TestL04A1, and TestL04Invariants, the E04 rules as
seven invariants over a seeded random walk of 200 jobs (invariants04.py).

Verify:

  make verify LESSON=04 REF=explore-it/lesson-03 -> DEFECTS REPRODUCED: 6 present
  (first REF attempt: PROBE ERROR U21, a probe ordering bug; retained with
  diagnostics)
  integration checks 61/61; unit tests pass; seeder A1 control ABSENT.
Dwell: paired only, U19-U23 and A1 PRESENT at lesson-03, ABSENT at lesson-04.

queuelet: fix experiment 05 findings; resolve A2; add checks (lesson 05)

Experiment 05 (Sequence it) used the verbs in unlikely pairs and triples,
then in a random walk that checked the rules after every step, and filed
three reports; the reconciliation made them unplanned U24-U26. All three
are fixed here, and the A2 spec silence is decided. The planned E05
defects (D12-D14) were fixed in E01 and held as sequences here.

Flaws, all at explore-it/lesson-04:
- U24 deleting a worker re-queued its leases without counting an attempt
  or writing an attempt row (api/jobs.go:126): max_attempts 2 delivered
  four times, each as attempt 1.
- U25 ack and cancel left lease_token, leased_by and an unexpired
  lease_expires_at on succeeded/cancelled rows (ack.go:10, operator.go:6).
- U26 the event trigger labelled any exit from leased lease_expired once
  last_error read "lease expired" (migrations/003.sql:21), so a later ack,
  cancel or worker release was logged as another expiry.
- A2 a job leased when its queue was purged went back to retry_wait on
  nack, into a queue the operator had just emptied.

Fix: expiry and worker deletion share one release path (internal/jobs
release): an attempt counted, a row written (expired / released), dead at
max; ack and cancel clear the three lease columns (ack takes the holder
from the pre-update row); the sweep marks its transaction with SET LOCAL
queuelet.release and the trigger reads that, not error text; purge sets
jobs.purge_requested (migrations/004.sql) on leased jobs, and nack or
release then dead-letters them; retry clears the mark.

Spec decisions (SPEC.md, README.md, register/reconciliations/05.md): a
worker-deletion release records an unsuccessful attempt like an expiry;
only a leased job has a lease token, holder and expiry, and attempt rows
keep the worker; an event is labelled with the new state except a release
by expiry; a job leased at a purge keeps its lease, ack completes it, and
a nack, expiry or worker deletion makes it dead. Left open: the attempt
row for a delivery cancelled in flight (with the cancel-while-running
silence).

Checks: TestL05U24..U26, TestL05A2, and TestL05Walk, 100 random verbs
asserting W1-W7 after every step (walk05.py). At lesson-04 the walk breaks
on W2/W3/W4 in every measured seed, but W1 (U24) never fired; U24 rests on
its own repro.

Flaws at explore-it/lesson-05:
- U27 schedule DELETE reports success for missing/repeated/foreign ids.
- U28 templates admit null/non-object payloads; cron and manual run disagree.
- U29 sample-worker echo rounds JSON numbers before result and webhook.
- U30 qctl rounds JSON input and display; shared option paths also affected.
- U31 NUL in result/error becomes a misleading 409 with driver text.
- U32 owner-race insert failures leak FK names as 400/500 instead of 404.
- U33 job removal leaves inaccessible attempt rows and error text behind.
- A4 is a policy silence, not an eighth blind finding; the sweep removes dead.

Fixes: share enqueue object/default validation with schedule creation;
check deleted schedule rows; UseNumber in client and qctl decoders;
adapt worker numeric consumers and baseline ID parsing without changing
behavioral assertions; reject NUL strings/keys before lease mutation;
map the two assigned owner FK violations in enqueue/schedule-create and
shared insertJob siblings; cascade attempt deletion from its job with a
guarded NOT VALID FK and supporting index; exempt dead from retention.

A4 decision: dead jobs remain until operator retry or explicit deletion; automatic retention applies only to succeeded and cancelled.
U33 decision: attempts belong to their job and leave on deletion, purge and retention; job events and pending webhook snapshots keep independent lifetimes.
U28 clarification: schedule create follows enqueue payload semantics (omitted {}, explicit null/non-object invalid); PATCH gains no payload field.
U31 clarification: NUL result/error is 400 invalid_result/invalid_error, leaving a valid lease usable.
